pages.text: The Decay Chamber takes a single particle beam and lets it fall apart, splitting heavier particles into lighter constituents. Where the Target Chamber builds things up, the Decay Chamber takes them apart.

pages.title: Construction
pages.text: Like all $(l:particle_chambers/general#construction)particle chambers$(/l), it is a hollow cube of casing or glass with odd, equal sides, from 5x5x5 up to 11x11x11. At the center sits a Particle Chamber Camera, joined to a Particle Chamber Beam Port on each of the 4 horizontal faces by a line of Particle Beam blocks.

pages.title: Ports
pages.text: One beam port runs in input mode to receive the beam; the others run in output mode and carry away the lighter particles split out of it. Shift right-click a beam port with a Multitool to switch its mode.$(br2)Add at least one Particle Chamber Port for energy, plus optional item and fluid ports.

pages.title: Detectors
pages.text: Like all $(l:particle_chambers/general#detectors)particle chambers$(/l), detectors placed inside raise the chamber's efficiency at the cost of power, scaling the recipe cross-section.

pages.title: Operation
pages.text: A decay recipe takes one incoming particle stack - a type, a minimum energy and an amount - and yields several lighter particles. Browse JEI for the full list and the energies involved. (Entropy, for once, working for you.)
